idiom_name: narrow view struct with json tags (the type is the filter)
implementation_notes: In Go the projection is a type, not an object: declare a small struct containing exactly the fields the receiver needs and marshal that instead of the domain struct, so encoding/json emits only the declared fields and a field that has no member in the view cannot leak; json:"-" marks a field the domain type still hides, and json:"name,omitempty" drops it when it is empty. What replaces the classic filter object is the view type plus a conversion function (or a View() method on the domain type) - the compiler then keeps the projection honest when the domain struct changes. Filtering a map[string]any with delete(...) or a key whitelist is still justified only when the field set is genuinely dynamic per request; used as the default it throws away exactly the type safety that made the Go realization idiomatic.
pitfalls: Deleting keys from a map[string]any needs no compile-time contract at all: a renamed source field yields a silently shorter message, so reserve map filtering for genuinely dynamic field sets.
Using the domain struct with json:"-" tags for one receiver couples the domain model to that receiver's view; adding a second receiver means tagging fields for both - use distinct view types instead.
omitempty also drops legitimate zero values (0, false, ""), so the receiver cannot distinguish 'absent' from 'zero' unless the wire type uses pointers or explicit presence.
An anonymous struct literal built inline per call site compiles and ships every field it mentions: nothing enforces that the view stays free of internal data across edits.
